versions.changelog:
- Removes the global `--default-quiet-hours` mechanism and the `--defaults` command. Quiet hours are per-reminder only.
- Adds `POKE_NOW_OVERRIDE` (ISO timestamp env var) for deterministic clock injection at deliver time.
- Adds `--reply-stdin`: reads reply text from stdin so it never lands in shell history, `ps`, or argv logs.
- Adds `POKE_ALLOW_REMOTE_OLLAMA=1` opt-in for non-loopback vector-tone endpoints; localhost-only otherwise.
- Drops the duplicate `presets/{en,cn}/` and `tones/{en,cn}/` locale folders (root files unchanged).

pokecron 1.0.2 — Security update

- SECURITY: Command hooks no longer inherit the full parent process.env.
  Hooks (--pre-cmd/--post-cmd/--on-pong-command/--if-unconfirmed-command)
  now run with a minimal base env (PATH, HOME, USER, LOGNAME, SHELL, LANG,
  LC_ALL, TZ) plus the documented POKE_* vars — closing the ambient
  secret/token exposure where any configured hook could read credentials
  that happened to be in the environment.
- Added --hook-env VAR (repeatable): default is now deny; this is the
  explicit allowlist to opt an individual parent var back into a hook
  when it genuinely needs one.
- Added a capabilities manifest to SKILL.md metadata (filesystem,
  process, environment, optional network) for transparent declaration.
- Renamed skill from "poke" to "pokecron".
- Added a regression test covering the hook-env allowlist behavior.
- Updated stages.md to document the minimal-env model and --hook-env.
- Version updated to 1.0.2.

- Expanded description to clarify that persisted timers use OS-native scheduling (systemd/launchd/Task Scheduler) and run local commands and prompts without a daemon.
- Added note on command hooks, listing supported hook flags and emphasizing security considerations when running local scripts.
- No functional or file changes; this update improves documentation for clarity and guidance.

Initial release — replaces heartbeat polling with reliable, reply-aware reminders and deferred agent tasks.

- OS-scheduled reminders and agent tasks: no daemons, no polling required (systemd/launchd/Task Scheduler support).
- Fast reply matching: forwards user responses to auto-cancel, snooze, or confirm reminders.
- Robust reminder creation, listing, management, and history—stateless delivery with local tracking.
- Cross-platform support (Linux, macOS, Windows).
- Modular design: sub-skills available for escalation, quiet hours, multi-channel, commitments, and more.
- All state and history managed locally under `.runtime/`, no cloud storage required.
